title: Clone the dominant motion, ignore the jitter
when: Learning a camera move or a subject's motion from a reference clip or a described move.
summary: Most of the motion in a clip is carried by a few dominant components (the camera's pan, push or tilt, the subject's main path); the rest is noise or tiny movement. To reuse a move, describe and rebuild only the dominant components.
do: Describe a reference move by its dominant parts: the camera's direction, its speed curve and its distance; the subject's main path and timing.
Rebuild those parts with the program's own camera moves and paths, timed to the narrator's words.
Keep camera motion and subject motion apart: clone one without the other when the story needs it.
avoid: Copying every wobble of a reference (handheld noise reads as a fault in a drawn world).
Copying a reference's content or look; only the motion is learned.
source: LPengYang/MotionClone, pinned 8b3d937 (MotionClone, arXiv 2406.05338): the paper's finding that a few dominant temporal-attention components carry the motion, restated as an editing idea; no code used (no licence file).

title: Split a reference into scenes at its visual jumps
when: Studying a reference video or competitor clip the owner provides, frame by frame.
summary: A reference is studied scene by scene. Cut it where the picture jumps, and sample each scene's frames so short effects are not missed: its first and last frame, each visual jump with the frame before and after it, then frames spread evenly across the rest.
steps: Scan every frame for visual jumps (cuts, flashes, fast moves).
Cut scenes near jumps rather than at fixed lengths.
Sample each scene: its first and last frame, every jump with its neighbours, then fill evenly.
Read the timestamps of the samples: they are not equally spaced.
avoid: Even sampling that skips a late flash or a short effect.
Interpolating a mask or a move across a real cut.
source: blixvip/MotionClone, pinned 9873ef2: app/scene_pipeline.py and app/ai.py, its reference-rebuild method restated; no code copied (no project-wide licence).

title: Compare the rebuild to the reference and keep only improvements
when: Matching a designed shot or a style to a reference, and deciding whether a correction helped.
summary: A rebuild is judged against its reference at the same timestamps, per colour channel (grayscale can pass the wrong palette). Only the worst scenes get a correction, a correction is kept only if it improves the match without making any frame much worse, and the earlier version is kept otherwise.
steps: Render the rebuild and compare it to the reference at the same times, per colour channel.
Correct only the two worst scenes, with the reference and rebuild frames side by side.
Keep a correction only if the average match improves and no frame gets clearly worse; otherwise keep the earlier version.
Say candidly what could not be rebuilt (photographs, complex 3D, footage).
avoid: Claiming a one-to-one match because every layer exists.
source: blixvip/MotionClone, pinned 9873ef2: app/scene_pipeline.py (similarity, bounded correction pass), its reference-rebuild method restated; no code copied (no project-wide licence).

title: Rebuild from editable layers, never by replaying the source
when: Designing a shot after a reference (a competitor's look, a style study).
summary: A rebuild is made of its own layers (type, shapes, drawings, measured motion), never of the source's frames or full-frame screenshots; small isolated artwork is the only raster allowed. That keeps it original and editable.
do: Rebuild typography, layout, panels, shapes and motion from scratch in the video's own art direction.
Use many measured key moments where position or scale changes; separate discontinuous scenes into separate layers.
Keep the layer count bounded (tens, not hundreds) per scene.
avoid: Embedding a reference's frames, footage or screenshots.
Replacing detailed artwork with emoji or generic placeholders.
source: blixvip/MotionClone, pinned 9873ef2: app/ai.py and app/rebuild_author.py (guides), app/reconstruction.py (audit), its reference-rebuild method restated; no code copied (no project-wide licence).
